aspects.says: RandomGeneratorFactory.of(name) picks an algorithm by name, and all() lists the ones the JVM has, so availability is checked first.

aspects.says: A shared Random suffers contention across threads, and the new algorithms are not thread-safe, so each thread gets its own generator.
basis: section:Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them
aspects.reason: contention is a performance effect and a data race on a generator is not reproducible, so no deterministic test can grade it

aspects.says: ints(count, origin, bound) streams count values from origin inclusive to bound exclusive, and a negative count throws IllegalArgumentException.
A JumpableGenerator's jump() moves to a statistically independent subsequence, so chunks drawn between jumps suit parallel work.

aspects.says: Java 17 is a long-term support release, supported by vendors until at least 2029.

aspects.says: RandomGenerator is the common interface of Random, SecureRandom, SplittableRandom, ThreadLocalRandom and the new algorithms, so an API takes it as its parameter type.
Sealed classes, final in Java 17, name their permitted subtypes, which lets a switch over them be exhaustive.
basis: section:Q3: What are sealed classes and how do they enable exhaustive pattern matching?

aspects.says: A sealed class must have at least one permitted subclass.
aspects.reason: a compile-time rule with no runtime behaviour to grade
